Here is the issue description:
# [dv] Out of bounds access in dside access tracking logic
This line: https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/blob/056cb44ff75f797898709546ea1b0fd08d862e1a/rtl/ibex_top.sv#L1092
Uses `i - 1` and it's possible to evaluate this condition when `i == 0` giving an out of bounds access. This logic needs refactoring to more explicitly split out the `i == 0` case from the others to ensure this does not occur.
> estimate 1

Then, review the provided code snippets, identify all related locations that require inspection or modification to resolve the issue.

<analysis>
The reported issue is an out-of-bounds array access in the dside access tracking logic in `rtl/ibex_top.sv`. The problematic pattern is in the `always_comb` block that populates `pending_dside_accesses_d[i]`: for `i > 0`, it checks `pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i - 1].valid`, but the condition is nested under `if (data_req_o && data_gnt_i)` and the loop iterates from `i = 0`. Although the code guards the `i == 0` case in one branch, the `else if` uses `i - 1` and must be carefully reviewed for any path where `i == 0` could still be evaluated or for related logic that assumes the same indexing pattern.

The main location requiring inspection is the `g_dside_tracker` generate block in `rtl/ibex_top.sv`, specifically:
- the shifting logic for `pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i]`
- the insertion logic for `pending_dside_accesses_d[i]`
- the assertion that depends on `pending_dside_accesses_q[MaxOutstandingDSideAccesses-1]`
- the adjacent assertion on `pending_dside_accesses_q[0]`, which provides important behavioral context for the queue semantics

Since the issue is about array indexing and tracking logic, the relevant inspection range should include the complete data-side tracker block and the nearby assertions, because they define the intended structure of the pending-access queue and may need consistency with any refactoring of the index handling.

The snippets from `rtl/ibex_pkg.sv` are only parameter and typedef definitions and do not appear to contain the bug directly. They are relevant only as contextual dependencies if the size or semantics of `MaxOutstandingDSideAccesses` are defined there elsewhere, but within the provided snippets no direct modification target is visible in `ibex_pkg.sv`.

Therefore, the primary location is the `rtl/ibex_top.sv` block around lines 1099–1145. No other provided snippet shows the same indexing pattern or a functionally similar implementation that obviously requires modification.
</analysis>
